findings.title: Blocked email lookup is case-sensitive and bypassable
findings.body: BlockedEmail.should_block? queries BlockedEmail.where(email: email) without normalizing the address via Email.downcase/strip, and User creation passes params[:email] directly to User.new_from_params with no email normalization. An attacker can register using a case variant such as Bad@spamclub.com for a blocked bad@spamclub.com, or with surrounding whitespace, and the blocklist is bypassed. The unique validation/index is also case-sensitive, so multiple case variants can coexist. The previous domain restriction check used a case-insensitive regex, indicating normalization/case-insensitivity was expected here.

findings.title: match_count is non-atomic and increments multiple times per signup
findings.body: should_block? performs a read-modify-write on record.match_count and then saves the record. In UsersController#create, user.valid? is called before user.save (lines 168 and 172), and for a new record email_changed? remains true, so the email validator runs twice for a single blocked signup and increments match_count twice. Concurrent signup attempts can also lose increments because the update is not atomic. This corrupts match_count/last_match_at statistics and causes unnecessary DB writes. Use an atomic DB update or move the side effect out of validation.
